zh.html: Recursive、Naive 和 Apex 近期均宣称已实现“用 AI 研发 AI”。但在其公开的四份技术报告中（Recursive 的 First Steps 与 Flint、Naive 的 N0.5-Flash，以及 Apex-35B），AI 优化的客体始终是训练代码、GPU kernel、推理引擎或训练数据（各项指标均为厂商自报），而执行优化的 AI 系统自身从未发生改变。按学术界的界定，这类过程仅属于一个系统对另一个外部对象的非递归优化6,7，其改进机制依然由人类固定在模型外部8，尚不构成递归自我改进（RSI）。

对三个开源权重模型的拆解检验进一步印证了这一点。Apex 是在 Qwen3.6 基础上进行的全参数继续训练，其推理行文被整体替换为类似 Claude 的风格推断；Naive 基于小米 MiMo-V2.5 的对话版继续训练，其中 9 层注意力权重几乎被重写；Flint 虽为从零训练，但其推理思维链中却直接出现了 "as a Gemini model" 等字样9,10。三款模型的底层基座或推理习惯均深度依赖外部现有模型，仅凭公开材料，无法剥离出它们的能力究竟有多少真正源于自动化研发管线与自动数据收集。

尽管学术界对 RSI 尚无公认的形式化定义11，但多数理论工作都要求同时满足两个条件：其一，改进机制位于系统内部，且能被系统自身改写12,7,8；其二，改进收益能够跨代累积，使系统改进的速度一代比一代快13,14,15,16——即 Yampolskiy 所说的“越改越会改”（gets better at getting better）7。在实证层面，迄今尚无研究真正跨越这一门槛。让模型用自身生成的数据反复重训，往往在寥寥数轮内便会陷入停滞甚至退化17,18,19；在本报告检索的约 96 份文献中，没有任何一项实验测出过后继代际的改进速度超越前代。

此前最接近这一目标的实证测试来自 Weco 的 AIDE²20。在该实验中，一个“教练” agent 负责反复改写“研究” agent 的代码，并仅保留能提升隐藏测试集平均得分（越高越好）的改动。主实验里，研究 agent 的得分从 0.703 升至 0.778，超越了人工编写的基线 agent（0.749）。随后，研究团队将这个改进后的 agent 提拔为新教练，与人工设计的教练各自运行 3 轮（每轮 50 步）进行对比，两者的最终平均分定格在 0.780 对 0.782，作者据此判定两者表现难分伯仲。不过，该测试改写的仅是外围脚手架代码，底层大语言模型的权重并未改变20。

本报告将这一测试从代码层面推进至模型权重层面。首先，让 Qwen3.5-9B 独立开展 3 小时研究（共 72 次尝试），它将 NanoChat 小模型的验证损失从 1.4152 降至 1.2308（每字节比特数 BPB，越低越好）1，证实了单代 AI 辅助研究本身确实有效。随后，用它在探索中被采纳的成功尝试记录微调其自身权重，如此逐代迭代产生三代后继模型，并在 8 个未曾见过的小型研究任务上横向比较各代模型的改进速度。

实验结果显示，三代后继模型的改进速度均未超过原始模型1,4。其中，第一代后继模型略慢于原始模型，且与使用“失败尝试记录”微调出的安慰剂（placebo）模型表现相当，说明模型并未真正学到哪些改进思路有效；第二代未能超越原始模型，第三代低于第二代，但这一差异尚未达到预设的显著性标准。补充实验显示，第一轮配方换种子重训后得分仍为 0.602，与原结果 0.605 接近；第三轮的下降因此不能归因于一般的随机训练波动。事实上，全篇实验统计上站得住的两个显著结论均为负面。第一个便是：如果不改权重，而是让模型阅读自身的历史记录、总结出经验笔记传给下一轮，其改进速度反而大幅下降约三分之一，表现甚至不如直接给出一份通用建议。
最后一组实验将“如何训练自己”的决策权也一并交还给模型：让它自主审阅历史尝试记录，自行决定筛选哪些样本、采用何种超参数进行微调。第一轮产出的模型，是所有经自身记录微调的模型中唯一一个改进速度略快于原始模型的，同时也快于按固定配方训练的第一代模型；但这两项优势均落在统计误差范围内，且未能胜过随机抽取同等数量记录的对照组1,21。
在启动第二轮之前，原始模型接收到了第一轮的正向反馈（即它在训练任务上的改进速度超过了原始模型）。然而它并未沿着这一方向继续推进，反而将训练配方改得极度保守——仅筛选出 137 条记录，并以极小的学习率训练了两个 epoch，导致模型权重几乎未发生改变，测试表现也随之退回至原始模型的水平。因此，在前两轮由原始模型主导的配方探索中，没有任何一组对比展现出统计显著的提升1,22。
第三轮由第一轮微调后的模型设计配方，得分降至 0.392，显著低于原始模型（0.588）和第二轮模型（0.595）。换种子重训第一轮配方后得分为 0.602，表明第一轮与第三轮的差距不能由随机种子波动解释。另以 Qwen3.8-27B 设计配方，得分为 0.513，未超过原始模型。整体结果表明，自主设计配方尚未带来可靠的跨代加速，且筛选规则与训练强度会显著影响结果1,3。

en.html: Overview. Does swapping in a successor speed up improvement? Each row represents one self-update approach; the dot marks its difference in improvement speed relative to the original model (Qwen3.5-9B), the horizontal bar shows the 95% confidence interval, and the grey band indicates the baseline noise when the same model runs twice (±2 SD). A dot to the left of 0 means slower than the original model. All data are measured across 8 unseen micro-research tasks; hover over any row for exact values1,3.

en.html: Recursive, Naive, and Apex have all recently claimed that they are using AI to build AI. Yet across their four public releases (Recursive's *First Steps* and *Flint*, Naive's *N0.5-Flash*, and *Apex-35B*), the targets of AI optimization are consistently training scripts, GPU kernels, inference engines, and synthetic training data—with all headline figures self-reported by the vendors—while the AI system performing the optimization remains unchanged. In the academic literature, this setup constitutes non-recursive optimization: one system optimizing a separate target6,7 under an improvement mechanism fixed externally by human engineers8. It does not yet qualify as recursive self-improvement (RSI).

Direct forensic checks of the three open-weight models reinforce this picture. Apex is a full-parameter continued training run on Qwen3.6 whose reasoning style has been wholesale replaced with patterns resembling Claude's (an inference). Naive continues training from the chat release of Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5, nearly rewriting 9 of its attention layers. Flint was trained from scratch, yet its reasoning traces occasionally leak phrases such as "as a Gemini model"9,10. Because the foundational weights or reasoning habits of all three models derive from existing external models, the public materials alone cannot isolate how much of their capability genuinely stems from automated R&D pipelines or automated data curation.

While academia still lacks a consensus formal definition of RSI11, most theoretical frameworks converge on two requirements: first, the improvement mechanism must reside inside the system and be open to self-modification12,7,8; second, the resulting gains must compound across generations so that each generation improves faster than the last13,14,15,16—a system that, in Yampolskiy's words, "gets better at getting better"7. Empirically, no system has crossed this threshold. Models trained repeatedly on their own synthetic outputs typically plateau or degrade within a few iterations17,18,19, and across roughly 96 sources reviewed for this report, none has ever measured one generation improving faster than its predecessor.

The closest empirical test to date is Weco's AIDE²20. In that setup, a "coach" agent iteratively rewrites the code of a "research" agent, retaining only modifications that raise the research agent's average score across a suite of tasks evaluated on held-out test data (where higher is better). In the primary run, this score climbed from 0.703 to 0.778, surpassing a hand-crafted baseline agent at 0.749. The improved agent was then promoted to serve as the new coach and pitted against the hand-crafted coach across 3 runs of 50 iterations each, finishing at 0.780 versus 0.782—a tie the authors deemed inconclusive. Moreover, only the scaffolding code changed during that test; the underlying language model weights remained frozen20.

This report extends the same test from scaffolding code to model weights. First, Qwen3.5-9B conducted autonomous research for 3 hours across 72 attempts, lowering the validation loss of a small NanoChat model from 1.4152 to 1.2308 bits per byte (where lower is better)1—confirming that single-generation AI-assisted research works. The model was then fine-tuned on its own accepted research trajectories generation after generation to produce three successive descendants, with each generation's speed of improvement measured across 8 held-out micro-research tasks.

None of the three successors improved faster than the original model1,4. The first generation was slightly slower, and a placebo model trained on rejected trajectories performed just as well, indicating that the model failed to learn which research ideas actually worked. The second generation failed to surpass the original model, while the third did not outperform the original model. The first is that when the model read its own history and distilled a note of lessons learned for the next run without updating its weights, its speed of improvement fell by roughly a third, performing worse than a generic list of tips.

A final set of experiments handed control over the training recipe to the model itself: it inspected its own attempt logs and decided which trajectories to filter and which hyperparameters to use for fine-tuning. Round 1 yielded the only self-tuned checkpoint that improved slightly faster than both the original model and the first-generation checkpoint trained under the fixed recipe. Both margins, however, fell within statistical noise, and the checkpoint failed to beat a control tuned on an equal number of randomly sampled records1,21.

Before round 2 began, the base model was shown the positive feedback from round 1—namely, that it had improved faster than the original model on the training tasks. Rather than building on that momentum, it pivoted to an ultra-conservative recipe, selecting just 137 records and training for two epochs at a tiny learning rate. As a result, the weights barely moved and performance regressed to the baseline level of the original model. Across the first two rounds, not a single comparison achieved statistical significance1,22.

Round 3 tested genuine recursion: the model fine-tuned in round 1 took over designing the next recipe, given the exact same feedback provided in round 2. Although it kept round 1's recipe nearly intact—adding only a 1% improvement threshold—the resulting model's improvement-speed score dropped from 0.605 in round 1 to 0.392, falling 0.197 below the original model (95% CI [−0.363, −0.050]) and significantly below round 2. A follow-up retraining of the Round-1 recipe with a new random seed scored 0.602, close to the original 0.605. The Round-3 decline therefore reflects the recipe and training conditions rather than ordinary seed variation. A Qwen3.8-27B-designed recipe scored 0.513, below the original model. Together, these results show that recipe design did not produce reliable acceleration, and that data selection and training intensity strongly shaped the outcome1,5.

zh.html: 递归自我改进（recursive self-improvement，RSI）的设想最早可以追溯到 1965 年。I. J. Good 当时提出，既然设计机器本身是一项智力活动，那么一台在所有智力活动上都超越人类的机器，理应也能设计出更好的机器；新一代机器如法炮制，便会引发“智能爆炸”（intelligence explosion）23。然而这一概念提出了六十年，学界至今仍未就其严格定义达成共识——就连 ICLR 2026 专门为 RSI 举办的研讨会，最终也没有给出形式化定义11。

争议首先在于如何界定“递归”。Yudkowsky 以此区分了两类过程：只有当执行优化的主体与被优化的对象相同时（例如 AI 重新设计自身的认知算法），过程才算递归；若仅仅是一个部件去优化另一个部件，则属于非递归优化（non-recursive optimization）6,7。他用存款作比：利息用于消费，财富仅呈线性增长；利息用于再投资，财富才会按复利累积。按此标准，自然选择与人类文明虽然都在积累，但人类大脑本身并未被改写，因此都属于前一类。不过，即便满足了“修改自身”的条件，改进也未必能持续——早期的 EURISKO 与优化编译器确实在改进自身，但都很快停滞6。

图 1 两种改进。(a) 改进者保持不变，反复改进另一个对象，对应 non-recursive optimization6。该面板回放一次真实运行：Qwen3.5-9B 在 3 个并行线程中改进 NanoChat 的训练脚本，共 72 次尝试；每次尝试依次经过提出补丁、沙箱训练、封存评估、保留或丢弃1,2。(b) 改进者改进自身：每一代完整运行一次 (a)，用留下的记录更新自己，再由下一代接替6,7；各代用时为假设值，用于示意"越改越会改"。(c) 回报率 r 决定进展是否加速：研发由 AI 完成时，r = 0.5 时每次翻倍所需时间变长（软件效率随时间线性增长，对应利息用于消费），r = 1 时每次翻倍所需时间相同，r > 1 时每次翻倍所需时间缩短，并在有限时间内发散15,16；曲线和翻倍点由公式计算。
Yampolskiy 将系统对自身的修改按深度分为三级7：

head: 级别
含义
原文的例子
rows: 在固定的目标下优化参数
越改越会改（gets better at getting better），能反复把旧方法换成全新的方法

zh.html: 最高一级要求系统不仅能优化自身，还能反复替换改进自身所用的方法。以超级编译（supercompilation，一种追踪原程序所有可能运行过程、借此剔除冗余计算并编译出等价新程序的变换技术24）为例：将其应用于自身时，第一轮约有 20% 的提升，第二轮仅提升约 3%，此后便不再产生增益。至于单纯增加内存或硬件，由于系统改进自身的能力并未改变，更不属于自我改进7。
具体到判定标准上，各家的定义主要在以下四个维度上存在分歧：
改进方法的位置。 Schmidhuber 的 Gödel machine 允许系统改写自身的任何部分，包括用于证明改动有效的搜索程序本身12。Yampolskiy 以及 Tang 等人也以此为分界：只要改进方法固定在系统外部，过程就不算递归7,8。
改进的对象。 Chalmers 要求被放大的能力必须恰好是“产生下一代的能力”，并称之为自我放大的能力（self-amplifying capacity）14。这与 Yampolskiy 所说的“越改越会改”（gets better at getting better）相互呼应7。
改进的累积。 Yudkowsky、Chalmers，以及 Epoch 和 Forethought 的研究都强调，下一代带来的提升幅度不能小于上一代；否则收益递减，增长最终会停止13,14,15,16。
通用性门槛。 早期观点如 Good 和 Hall 认为，启动这一过程的前提是系统具备全面的通用性23,25；Chalmers 和 Yudkowsky 则放宽了要求，认为低于人类水平的系统同样可能跨过启动门槛14,13；Eth 和 Davidson 进一步将其收窄，认为系统只需在“AI 研发”这一特定领域内具备通用性即可16。
在本文检索到的文献中，Tang 等人在 2026 年给出了唯一一个形式化定义8。该定义完全以改进机制的位置划界：改进机制位于 agent 外部时，过程属于 GPI（一般的迭代策略改进）；机制内化于 agent 内部时，过程才属于 RSI。至于改进是否会加速，该定义并未预设，而是留作交由实验回答的问题。

若沿用这一内外部边界来审视当下的常见范式，自蒸馏（self-distillation）与自博弈（self-play）实则都停留在 weak self-improvement 一级：模型虽然自己产生训练数据，但训练流程与更新规则仍由人事先固定在系统外部推断。目前文献中尚无研究直接对自蒸馏定性，仅有 Mahoney 明确探讨过自博弈的归属。他虽然把自博弈归为自我改进，但也从理论上证明，在没有外部信息输入的前提下，第 n 代程序的复杂度最多按 log n 的速度增长26。

而改进过程能否真正加速，可以用回报率 r 来刻画。Epoch 和 Forethought 将 r 定义为：累积研发投入每翻一倍时，软件效率翻倍的次数15,16。当 r 大于 1 时，每次效率翻倍所需的投入递减，进展呈加速态势；当 r 小于 1 时，进展则逐渐放缓。从历史数据的估算来看，国际象棋引擎的 r 约为 0.8315，图像识别约为 1.4，线性规划约为 1.1，SAT 求解器约为 3.5，不过多数估计值在统计上并不显著16。Forethought 估计，在算力保持不变的前提下，软件的 r 介于 0.5 到 2 之间，而大语言模型目前尚无对应的估计值16。

落到实验层面，上述理论定义最终都归结为同一个可检验的问题：当被改进的后继者接替成为新的改进者时，改进的速度是否比上一代更快？Weco 将跨过这一临界点的时刻称为“点火”（ignition）27，AIDE² 也据此设计了专门的 ignition test20。类似地，HGM 通过评估后代的表现来衡量一个 agent 的改进能力，并将其称为元生产力（metaproductivity）28；STOP 的作者则明确指出，由于底层模型权重并未改变，他们的方法还算不上完整的递归自我改进（"not full recursive self-improvement"）29。
为了在实验中统一衡量这一差异，本报告借用导数的概念，将“性能的提升”与“改进性能的能力”明确区分开来：
一阶改进（first-order improvement） 衡量的是单代性能。改进者自身保持不变，仅被改进的对象持续变好；若以任务表现对尝试次数作图，表现为曲线的斜率为正。例如在本报告第 4 节的实验中，固定不变的 Qwen3.5-9B 将 NanoChat 的验证损失从 1.4152 降至 1.2308，这便属于典型的一阶改进1。四份报告所展示的成果，同样属于这一范畴。

二阶改进（second-order improvement） 衡量的则是改进能力本身。在同一组任务和相同的预算下，比较各代改进者的改进速度；只有当改进速度随代际更替而上升——即表现曲线的二阶导数为正时，才构成二阶改进。二阶改进对应了 Weco 所说的 ignition27，也是 Yampolskiy 所说“越改越会改”的可测量形式7。在回报率模型中，二阶改进大致对应于 r ≥ 1 的区间，但两者并不完全等价：r 是按累积投入定义的，而二阶改进则是按代际之间的差值定义的推断15,16。

在实际应用这一标准时，还需注意两个前提。首先，度量尺度必须事先固定，因为正如 Chalmers 所指出的，对同一组实验数据换用不同的尺度（例如从对数尺度换为线性尺度），可能会得出完全相反的结论14。其次，观察到寥寥几代的二阶改进，并不意味着加速能够无限持续：Benthall 以及 Davidson 和 Houlden 都预测，当系统逐渐逼近上限时，改进速度终将回落30,31。基于此，本报告将“是否实现二阶改进”作为区分真正 RSI 与一般 AI 辅助研发的操作性标准：第 2 节将用这一标尺剖析现有的四份报告，第 4 节的实验也将围绕它展开。

en.html: The idea of recursive self-improvement (RSI) dates back to 1965. I. J. Good argued that because designing machines is itself an intellectual activity, a machine that surpasses humans across all intellectual activities could also design better machines; each new generation would then design an even better one, setting off an "intelligence explosion"23. Six decades later, however, the field still lacks an agreed definition—even the ICLR 2026 workshop devoted specifically to RSI stopped short of offering a formal one11.

The first point of contention lies in what makes a process "recursive." Yudkowsky uses the term to separate two distinct regimes: a process is recursive only when the entity doing the optimizing and the object being optimized are one and the same, as when an AI redesigns its own cognitive algorithms; when one component merely optimizes another, the process is non-recursive optimization6,7. He compares the difference to savings: spending the interest yields linear growth in wealth, whereas reinvesting it yields compound growth. By this standard, both natural selection and human civilization accumulate gains without rewriting the human brain itself, placing them in the first category. Yet merely modifying oneself is no guarantee of sustained progress—early systems such as EURISKO and optimizing compilers do improve themselves, but both stall quickly6.

Figure 1. Two kinds of improvement. (a) A fixed improver repeatedly improves a different object, which corresponds to non-recursive optimization6. The panel replays a real run: Qwen3.5-9B improving NanoChat training code in 3 parallel threads over 72 attempts, each going through patch proposal, sandbox training, sealed evaluation, and keep or discard1,2. (b) The improver improves itself: each generation runs (a) once, updates itself from the records, and hands over to the next6,7; generation times are assumed and illustrate getting better at getting better. (c) The rate of return r determines whether progress accelerates. With research done by AI, each doubling takes longer when r = 0.5 (software efficiency grows linearly over time, like spending the interest), every doubling takes the same time when r = 1, and doublings get shorter with a finite-time blow-up when r > 115,16; curves and doubling marks are computed from the equations.
Yampolskiy divides self-modification into three levels of depth7:

head: Level
Meaning
Example in the source
rows: the system changes itself without getting better
parameters are optimized under a fixed objective
the system gets better at getting better, and can repeatedly replace old methods with entirely new ones

en.html: Reaching the highest level requires a system not just to tune itself, but to repeatedly replace the very methods by which it improves. Consider supercompilation—a program transformation that traces the possible execution paths of an original program and compiles an equivalent version with redundant computations stripped out24. When applied to itself, supercompilation yields roughly a 20% speedup on the first pass and about 3% on the second, before flatlining entirely. Simply adding memory or hardware, meanwhile, does not count as self-improvement at all, because the system's underlying capacity to improve itself remains unchanged7.
Across the literature, competing definitions diverge mainly along four dimensions:

Where the improvement method sits. Schmidhuber's Gödel machine allows the system to rewrite any part of itself, including the proof-search program that verifies whether a change is beneficial12. Yampolskiy, as well as Tang and colleagues, draw the same boundary: as long as the improvement mechanism remains fixed outside the system, the process is not recursive7,8.

What is improved. Chalmers requires that the capacity being amplified be specifically the capacity to produce the next generation—what he terms a self-amplifying capacity14. This directly echoes Yampolskiy's criterion that the system "gets better at getting better"7.

Whether gains accumulate. Yudkowsky, Chalmers, and researchers at Epoch and Forethought all require that each generation deliver at least as much improvement as the one before it; otherwise, diminishing returns set in and growth eventually halts13,14,15,16.

Generality. Early accounts by Good and Hall assume the system must possess full generality to start the loop23,25. Chalmers and Yudkowsky relax this threshold, arguing that a sub-human system could also initiate the process14,13. Eth and Davidson narrow the requirement further: the system need only be general within the domain of AI research itself16.

Among the works reviewed for this report, Tang and colleagues (2026) provide the only formal definition of RSI8. Their formulation hinges entirely on the locus of the improvement mechanism: when the mechanism sits outside the agent, the process reduces to GPI (general iterative policy improvement); only when the mechanism is internalized within the agent does it qualify as RSI. Whether the resulting loop accelerates is left out of the definition itself and treated as an empirical question.

Judged by this internal-external boundary, common paradigms such as self-distillation and self-play fall under weak self-improvement: while the model generates its own training data, the training pipeline and update rules remain fixed in advance by human engineers (an inference). Although no source in the literature classifies self-distillation directly, Mahoney explicitly examines self-play. While he counts self-play as a form of self-improvement, he also proves that without external input, the complexity of the n-th generation can grow at most on the order of log n26.

Whether an improvement loop actually accelerates can be formalized through the rate of return r. Epoch and Forethought define r as the number of times software efficiency doubles for each doubling of cumulative research input15,16. When r exceeds 1, each subsequent doubling requires less input and progress accelerates; when r falls below 1, progress decelerates. Historical estimates place r at roughly 0.83 for computer chess15, 1.4 for image recognition, 1.1 for linear programming, and 3.5 for SAT solvers, though most of these estimates are not statistically significant16. Holding compute fixed, Forethought estimates r for software at between 0.5 and 2, with no specific estimate yet available for large language models16.

In experimental settings, these theoretical distinctions converge on a single testable question: when an improved successor takes over as the improver, does it drive progress faster than its predecessor did? Weco terms this threshold ignition27, a concept AIDE² operationalizes through its ignition test20. Along similar lines, HGM evaluates an agent's capacity to improve by the performance of its descendants—calling this metaproductivity28—while the authors of STOP explicitly note that because their underlying model weights remain frozen, their approach is "not full recursive self-improvement"29.
To evaluate these claims on a consistent footing, this report borrows the language of derivatives to separate gains in performance from gains in the ability to improve performance:

First-order improvement measures performance itself. Here, the improver remains fixed while the target object steadily improves; plotting task performance against the number of attempts yields a curve with a positive slope. In Section 4, for instance, a fixed Qwen3.5-9B model lowers the validation loss of NanoChat from 1.4152 to 1.2308—a clear case of first-order improvement1. The headline results across all four reports examined later also belong to this category.

Second-order improvement measures the ability to improve. Holding the task suite and budget constant across generations, the speed at which each generation of improver makes progress is compared; only when the rate of improvement increases from one generation to the next—meaning the second derivative of the performance curve is positive—does the process achieve second-order improvement. This criterion corresponds to Weco's notion of ignition27 and provides a measurable test for Yampolskiy's "gets better at getting better"7. In the rate-of-return framework, second-order improvement roughly aligns with the regime where r ≥ 1, though the two are not strictly identical: r is defined over cumulative input, whereas second-order improvement is defined over generational differences (an inference)15,16.

Applying this standard in practice requires two caveats. First, the scale of measurement must be fixed in advance; as Chalmers observes, rescaling the same data (for instance, between logarithmic and linear scales) can flip the conclusion entirely14. Second, observing second-order improvement across a few initial generations does not guarantee indefinite acceleration: both Benthall and Davidson and Houlden predict that improvement speeds will eventually taper off as a system approaches its limits30,31. With those caveats in place, this report adopts second-order improvement as the operational line separating genuine RSI from ordinary AI-assisted research: Section 2 uses it to audit the four reports, and the experiments in Section 4 are designed around it.

zh.html: Recursive：First Steps Toward Automated AI Research

Recursive 的自动化研究系统在三个公开基准上展示了优化成果。在 NanoChat（要求单卡 GPU 在 5 分钟固定预算内训练一个小型语言模型）上，系统将验证集 BPB 从社区最优的 0.9372 降至 0.9109，相当于缩短了约 1.3 倍的训练时间即可达到同等损失38,39,40,41。在 NanoGPT Speedrun（以最短时间将验证损失训至 3.28）上，系统将耗时从 79.7 秒压缩至 77.5 秒42,43。在包含 235 个 GPU kernel 编写任务的 SOL-ExecBench 上，系统将平均得分从 0.699 提升至 0.75444,45,46。
在评测严谨性上，基线使用了 10 个随机种子进行评估，Speedrun 的结果也附带了显著性检验（p = 0.0078）47,48。针对另外两个从较弱起点出发的实验，作者也坦承底层模型在预训练阶段可能已经见过相关的公开优化技巧，因此不能直接视为系统的独立发现49。

然而在系统透明度与细节核对上，这份报告存在明显的盲区。Recursive 仅公开了最终搜出的解法本身（包括训练代码、各种子结果，以及 235 个 kernel 中的 10 个）50,51，但并未公开研究系统本身；报告中既未交代底层所用模型、迭代轮数与消耗算力，也未说明系统在运行中是否修改过自身的脚手架代码32。此外，SOL 部分的代码未附带正确性检查52；Speedrun 的成绩并未提交至官方排行榜，且博客正文与代码仓库给出的耗时存在出入（分别为 77.5 秒与 77.34 秒）53,54,55。通过检视仓库中的文件命名（例如编号排到 w204 的 kernel 变体以及 CROSSOVER 等标记），可以看出该系统在底层采用了进化式搜索策略56。
纵观这三项实验，被持续优化的对象始终是外部的训练脚本和 GPU kernel，而执行优化的研究系统自身则保持固定。按第 1 节的标准衡量，这属于典型的一阶改进。报告虽将 RSI 作为长期愿景提出，但并未给出任何二阶改进的测量。
Naive：N0.5-Flash、NaiveRT 与 AutoWM
Naive-N0.5-Flash 是一个在 MiMo-V2.5 基础上继续训练而成的 309B 参数 MoE 模型，每个 token 激活 15.5B 参数57,58。报告展示了 AI 参与研发的三个案例：稀疏注意力架构设计、推理引擎 NaiveRT，以及世界模型项目 AutoWM。

在架构优化上，N0.5-Flash 以 5:1 的比例混合了滑动窗口注意力与 DeepSeek Sparse Attention（DSA）59；其 DSA 索引器仅使用 16 个查询头，使索引选择的耗时比原版减少了 44%60,61。在推理引擎 NaiveRT 的开发中，人类研究员与 AI 模型协作，在六天内完成了构建62。开发日志共记录了 151 次优化尝试，其中 63 次被采纳，71 次因未通过验证或引入退化而被回滚63,64，最终将一次完整的投机解码耗时从 SGLang 下的 12.3 ms 压缩至 3.4 ms65。报告同时记录了一次失败尝试：团队共实现了七版 MoE 融合算子，尽管数值校验全部正确，但端到端性能反而下降，研究员最终叫停了这一方向66。
图 3　NaiveRT 三个阶段的优化尝试。151 次尝试中有 63 次被采纳；另外 88 次中，71 次未通过验证或被回滚，17 次属于探索性尝试。数字为 Naive 自报63,67,68,69,64。

zh.html: 在第三个案例 AutoWM 中，N0.5-Flash 亲自担任“AI 研究员”。经过 400 小时的累计自动研究，它在 WorldArena 基准上取得了 77.43 分，超越了当时已公布的最高成绩 73.64 分70,71,72,34。不过，AutoWM 直接使用目标评测指标本身来筛选输出，且报告并未拆解各个子模块对最终分数的独立贡献73。

报告还将 N0.5-Flash 与 Recursive 的系统进行了横向对比，宣称在 NanoChat 上以 0.9051 优于后者的 0.910974。但这项对比运行在 Naive 自建的研究框架下，且未报告随机种子数与方差33；而在 SOL-ExecBench 上，Naive 引用 Recursive 的得分为 67.56，Recursive 原报告自报的则是 0.754，两者口径并不一致75,46。

对公开权重的差分检验进一步揭示了报告未提及的细节。首先，N0.5-Flash 的直接父模型实为 MiMo-V2.5 的对话版（Chat），而非 Base 版。在被改造为稀疏注意力的 9 层网络中，q、k、v 投影矩阵接近被彻底重写（v 投影权重改动的中位数达 51.9%），模型还额外新增了 189 个索引器张量9。其次，报告声称“将 MLA 替换为了 GQA”，但查验 MiMo-V2.5 的原始权重可知，其本来使用的就是 GQA52。

zh.html: 在行为普查测试中，面对 80 条测试提示，N0.5-Flash 有 76 条以 "We need to…" 或 "We need answer…" 开启思维链，这与 Flint 在代码和数学题上的推理起手式高度一致；其思维链长度中位数仅为 553 个字符，在四个被测模型中最短9,76。这表明两个模型的后训练轨迹可能蒸馏自同一类外部教师模型；不过由于本报告尚未对 MiMo-V2.5 原模型做同样测试，目前也不能排除这种行文风格直接继承自父模型的可能推断。此外，在全部 104 条测试提示中，N0.5-Flash 从未提及 MiMo 或小米。它对自身身份的回答，首先源于聊天模板在缺失系统提示时自动注入的默认身份句，因此不能作为权重层面洗去了原模型身份的证据9。

zh.html: 从改进机制来看，NaiveRT 和稀疏注意力改写的是推理引擎与模型结构，均属一阶改进；而在 AutoWM 中，N0.5-Flash 虽然扮演了研究员角色，但它优化的对象是外部的世界模型而非自身。报告虽然设想由下一代模型接管更多研究工作，但并未提供代际之间的改进速度测量。
Recursive：Flint

Flint 是 Recursive 借助其自动化研究系统 Eureka Machine 从零训练的 MoE 模型，总参数量 40B，每个 token 激活 2.5B，研发耗时不到四个月77,78,79。在 M4 Pro 笔记本上，Flint 的解码速度超过每秒 125 个 token80。研究系统还将模型的输出层量化至 4 bit，使最终的 NVFP4 模型与 16-bit 满血版的性能差距控制在 0.7 分以内81,82。至于“新训练出的模型能否反过来提升研究系统本身”，报告仅将其表述为一项未来的押注（"Our bet is…"），且并未量化 Eureka Machine 在各个研发环节中的具体贡献比例35。

对本地权重的检验确认了其公开规格：实测总参数为 39.785B，激活参数为 2.515B83。其分词器确由 Recursive 独立训练，15 万个词表项中仅有 51 个接近未训练的初始状态，这与报告“从零训练”的说法相吻合10。不过在元数据上，模型存在几处自相矛盾：Flint 在对话中自报的知识截止时间为 2025 年 5 月，但官方模型卡写的却是 2026 年 6 月84；博客宣称上下文长度为 512k，而权重配置文件中实际设定为 262,14485,86。

更关键的发现来自后训练阶段的外部模型痕迹。在行为测试中，Flint 的思维链里直接出现了 "as a Gemini model…" 和 "Since I am a Google AI" 等原句；同时，它的推理文风呈现出明显的“按题型分流”特征：代码与数学题采用 gpt-oss 式的简短笔记体，知识问答与闲聊采用 Gemini 式的编号分步体，而中文提示词下的行文则高度接近 DeepSeek-R110。这些迹象表明，Flint 的后训练过程极可能按任务类别拼接了不同外部教师模型的蒸馏数据推断。
此外，同一模型在不同机构的评测框架下得分差异显著：Flint 在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上自报得分为 54.9%，而 Apex 用自身框架测得的结果为 59.6；在 SWE-Bench Pro v2 上，Flint 自报高达 89.7%，Apex 测得则为 85.287,88,89,90。

zh.html: 归结而言，Flint 只是 Eureka Machine 生产出的单代产物。无论是在幕后执行搜索的研究系统，还是在后训练中提供推理范式的外部教师模型，都不是 Flint 自身，因此它展示的依然是一阶改进。
Apex：Apex-35B-V1.0

Apex-35B 是在阿里 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 基础上继续训练的模型，总参数 35B，每个 token 约激活 3B93,94。报告中专设了题为 "Building Apex-35B-V1.0 Through Recursive Self-Improvement" 的一节，列举了多项优化收益：引入“自我进化”（self-evolving）数据后，内部基准 CFD-Bench 提升了 32.1 分（未说明具体单位）95；训练吞吐提升 45–60%，解码速度提升 1.6–1.8 倍，首 token 延迟降低 30–35%，但上述系统指标均未给出具体的对比基线96,97,98,99。此外，报告中的各项基准评测在每个任务上均只运行了一次37。

在展示模型自主研发能力的 AI4AI 一节中，Apex 亲自担任研究员，任务是在 4 小时探索与 12 小时重训的预算内，用 GRPO 算法训练 Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 玩推箱子（Sokoban）。训练后的小模型在 512 个未见关卡上达到了 24.4% 的解出率，正文将其宣传为“超过 base model（11.7%）的两倍”100,101,102。然而核对图注与导读记录可以发现，11.7% 其实是未经任何训练的 Qwen2.5-3B 初始得分（即被训练对象的起点），而非对照组研究员的成绩；事实上，作为对照的 Base 研究员在运行 101 分钟后便因故障退出，根本没有完成训练或提交结果103,104。因此，这项实验仅能证明 Apex 成功跑完了一次强化学习训练流程，并不能证明它作为研究员的能力优于基线模型。

权重层面的比对显示，Apex 的模型配置与分词器均与 Qwen3.6 逐字段完全一致，但全部权重张量都发生了变化52。这表明它经历了一次全参数继续训练：各个专家网络的权重改动幅度在 6% 至 21% 之间，路由器改动为 9%9。与此同时，模型的思考方式被整体重塑：原版 Qwen3.6 在 80 条测试提示中有 70 条以标志性的 "Here's a thinking process:" 开头，而 Apex 降为 0/80，转而在 72/80 的提示中以 "The user asks/wants…" 起手，且思维链长度缩短至原来的三分之一以下——这一特征与使用 Claude 风格的思维链进行蒸馏高度吻合，尽管 Apex 在回答中并未自称 Claude推断。当被直接问及身份时，Apex 会坦承自身的基座是 Qwen3.6；而在未挂载任何外部工具的裸测环境下，它仍会凭空尝试调用一个并不存在的 web_search 工具9。
尽管 Apex 直接将自身的构建过程冠以“递归自我改进”之名，但报告并未提供任何逐代演进的数据。其所谓的“自我进化”数据在分类上仅属于 weak self-improvement7，背后的训练框架与改进规则依然完全由人类工程师预先设计8。
共同点
综合上述模型解剖结果，这三个开放权重的模型在底层基座或高层思考方式上，均深度依赖外部现有模型：

head: Flint
Apex
Naive
rows: MiMo-V2.5 对话版，9 层注意力重写
随任务类别变化：简短写法、Gemini 式编号
统一为简短写法 "We need to…"
思考中出现 "as a Gemini model"

zh.html: （来源：9,10）

横向审视这四份材料，它们所展示的实质成果全部停留在一阶改进：算子 kernel 变得更快、训练脚本变得更高效、模型在特定基准上的得分变得更高。但没有任何一份报告真正完成了二阶改进的测量——即把改进所得的后继模型放回研发管线中接替担任改进者，在同等预算下检验其改进速度是否超越前代。不仅如此，即便是对一阶改进的衡量，不同团队在不同框架下测出的分数也往往相互打架（如 Flint 与 SOL-ExecBench 的跨报告分差）。为什么这个最核心的二阶测量在产业界报告中始终缺位？下一节将具体剖析其中的症结。

en.html: In 2026, Recursive, Naive, and Apex released four technical reports: Recursive's *First Steps* and *Flint*, Naive's *N0.5-Flash*, and Apex's *Apex-35B*. All four center on the role of AI in model development. This section cross-examines their claims using three sources of evidence: the statements in the reports themselves, the publicly released weights and code, and this report's own independent reproductions and forensic measurements. Unless noted otherwise, vendor figures cited below are self-reported.

en.html: Recursive: First Steps Toward Automated AI Research

Recursive evaluated its automated research system across three public benchmarks. On NanoChat—which requires training a small language model within a fixed five-minute budget on a single GPU—the system lowered validation BPB from the community best of 0.9372 to 0.9109, equivalent to reaching the same loss in roughly 1.3 times less training time38,39,40,41. On NanoGPT Speedrun, which measures the shortest time to reach a validation loss of 3.28, the system trimmed the record from 79.7 to 77.5 seconds42,43. On SOL-ExecBench, a suite of 235 GPU kernel-writing tasks, it raised the mean score from 0.699 to 0.75444,45,46.

From an evaluation standpoint, the baseline was tested across 10 random seeds, and the Speedrun result includes a statistical significance test (p = 0.0078)47,48. For two additional runs initialized from weaker starting points, the authors candidly note that the underlying model may have encountered the relevant public techniques during pre-training, meaning those runs should not be interpreted as independent discoveries49.

What the report leaves out, however, is the system itself. Recursive released only the final artifacts discovered—the training scripts, per-seed logs, and 10 of the 235 kernels50,51—without disclosing the underlying model, the number of search iterations, the total compute spent, or whether the system ever modified its own scaffolding32. Moreover, the released SOL kernels lack a correctness verification suite52, and the Speedrun result was never submitted to the official leaderboard, with the blog post and code repository citing slightly different times (77.5 vs. 77.34 seconds)53,54,55. Artifact naming conventions in the repository—such as kernel variants numbered up to w204 and tags like CROSSOVER—indicate that the harness relies on evolutionary search under the hood56.

Across all three benchmarks, the targets of optimization are external training scripts and GPU kernels, while the research system doing the optimizing remains fixed. By the criteria established in Section 1, these results represent first-order improvement. While the report frames RSI as a long-term ambition, it provides no second-order measurements.
Naive: N0.5-Flash, NaiveRT and AutoWM

Naive-N0.5-Flash is a 309B-parameter MoE model (15.5B active per token) built via continued training on MiMo-V2.557,58. Its report highlights three areas of AI-assisted development: a sparse-attention architecture, the NaiveRT inference engine, and the AutoWM world-model project.

On the architectural front, N0.5-Flash interleaves sliding-window attention with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) in a 5:1 ratio59; by restricting the DSA indexer to 16 query heads, it cuts index-selection latency by 44% compared to the original design60,61. For the NaiveRT engine, human researchers collaborated with AI models to complete the system in six days62. Development logs record 151 optimization attempts—63 adopted and 71 rolled back or rejected during validation63,64—ultimately cutting a full speculative-decoding step from 12.3 ms in SGLang to 3.4 ms65. The report also documents a dead end: seven distinct implementations of MoE kernel fusion all passed numerical checks but degraded end-to-end latency, prompting researchers to abandon the direction66.

en.html: In the third case, AutoWM, N0.5-Flash itself served as the AI researcher. Over 400 hours of cumulative autonomous experimentation, it achieved a score of 77.43 on WorldArena, surpassing the previous published high of 73.6470,71,72,34. However, AutoWM selects its outputs directly against the target evaluation metric, and the report does not isolate the contributions of individual pipeline components73.

The report also benchmarks N0.5-Flash directly against Recursive's system, claiming an edge of 0.9051 versus 0.9109 on NanoChat74. That comparison, however, was run inside Naive's own evaluation harness without reporting seed counts or variance33; meanwhile, on SOL-ExecBench, Naive cites Recursive's score as 67.56, whereas Recursive's own report states 0.75475,46.

A weight-diff analysis uncovers several structural details omitted from the report. First, N0.5-Flash descends from the chat-tuned release of MiMo-V2.5 rather than the Base checkpoint. Across the 9 layers converted to sparse attention, the q, k, and v projections were nearly rewritten from scratch—with a median weight change of 51.9% in the v projection—alongside 189 newly added indexer tensors9. Second, although the report claims to have "replaced MLA with GQA," inspecting the original MiMo-V2.5 weights confirms that the parent model already used GQA52.

en.html: In behavioral testing, N0.5-Flash opens its chain of thought with "We need to…" or "We need answer…" on 76 out of 80 census prompts, closely mirroring Flint's phrasing on coding and math tasks; its median reasoning trace is just 553 characters, the shortest among the four models audited9,76. This convergence suggests that both models may have been distilled from a similar class of external teacher traces—though because the same census was not run on MiMo-V2.5, the possibility cannot be ruled out that the phrasing was inherited from the parent checkpoint (inference). Across all 104 test prompts, N0.5-Flash never mentions MiMo or Xiaomi. Its responses to identity queries stem primarily from a default identity string injected by the chat template whenever no system prompt is supplied, providing no evidence of weight-level identity erasure9.

en.html: Assessed against the framework of Section 1, both NaiveRT and the sparse-attention modifications target the inference engine and model architecture, placing them squarely in first-order improvement. In AutoWM, N0.5-Flash does act as the researcher, yet the object it optimizes is a separate world model rather than itself. While the report envisions future generations taking over a larger share of R&D, it offers no generation-over-generation measurements.
Recursive: Flint

Flint is a 40B-parameter MoE model (2.5B active per token) trained from scratch in under four months using Recursive's automated research system, the Eureka Machine77,78,79. Running locally on an M4 Pro laptop, it decodes at over 125 tokens per second80. The research system also quantized the output head to 4 bits, keeping the final NVFP4 checkpoint within 0.7 points of the 16-bit baseline81,82. As for closing the loop—having the newly trained model improve the research system in return—the report frames this strictly as a future bet ("Our bet is…") and does not quantify how much the Eureka Machine contributed to each stage of Flint's creation35.

Inspecting the local weights confirms the published architectural specs: 39.785B total parameters and 2.515B active83. Recursive also trained a custom tokenizer in which only 51 of the 150,000 vocabulary entries remain near their untrained initialization, consistent with a from-scratch training run10. Several metadata fields, however, conflict with one another: the model claims a knowledge cutoff of May 2025 in conversation while the model card lists June 202684, and the blog advertises a 512k context window whereas the configuration file sets the limit at 262,14485,86.

More revealing are the footprints left by external models during post-training. In this report's behavioral probes, Flint's reasoning traces occasionally leak verbatim phrases such as "as a Gemini model…" and "Since I am a Google AI". Furthermore, its reasoning style shifts sharply by task category: coding and math prompts trigger terse, gpt-oss-style notes; general knowledge and chat prompts elicit Gemini-style numbered steps; and Chinese prompts produce reasoning patterns closely resembling DeepSeek-R110. Together, these artifacts indicate that post-training relied on routing different task types to distinct external teacher models for distillation (inference).

Benchmark scores also shift depending on who runs the evaluation. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Recursive self-reports 54.9% for Flint while Apex's harness measures 59.6; on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Recursive reports 89.7% whereas Apex measures 85.287,88,89,90.

en.html: Ultimately, Flint is the output of a research pipeline, not its driver. Neither the Eureka Machine that searched over its design nor the external teacher models that supplied its reasoning traces are Flint itself, making it another instance of first-order improvement.
Apex: Apex-35B-V1.0

Apex-35B (35B total parameters, ~3B active per token) was built via continued training on Alibaba's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B93,94. A section of the report titled "Building Apex-35B-V1.0 Through Recursive Self-Improvement" attributes several gains to "self-evolving" data: a 32.1-point jump on the internal CFD-Bench (with no unit specified)95, a 45–60% increase in training throughput, a 1.6–1.8× decoding speedup, and a 30–35% reduction in time to first token—all reported without baseline figures96,97,98,99. Every benchmark result in the report is also based on a single evaluation run per task37.

In the report's AI4AI section, Apex steps into the role of researcher: given a budget of 4 hours for exploration and 12 hours for retraining, it is tasked with training Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct via GRPO to play Sokoban. The resulting student model solves 24.4% of 512 held-out levels, a figure the main text highlights as more than double "the base model's 11.7%"100,101,102. Checking the figure caption, however, reveals that 11.7% is merely the zero-shot score of the untrained Qwen2.5-3B student model—not the score achieved by a baseline researcher. In fact, the comparison "Base" researcher crashed and exited after 101 minutes without finishing training or submitting a checkpoint103,104. The experiment therefore demonstrates only that Apex managed to complete a training run without crashing, not that it outperforms a baseline model at conducting AI research.

Weight inspection confirms that Apex shares Qwen3.6's exact configuration schema and tokenizer, while every weight tensor has been updated52. Specifically, full-parameter continued training shifted individual expert weights by 6% to 21% and router weights by 9%9. Post-training also completely overwrote the model's reasoning habits: whereas Qwen3.6 opens 70 of 80 census prompts with "Here's a thinking process:", Apex never uses that phrase (0/80), opening instead with "The user asks/wants…" on 72 of 80 prompts and producing reasoning traces less than a third as long—a pattern consistent with distillation from Claude-style traces, though Apex never claims to be Claude (inference). When asked directly, Apex identifies Qwen3.6 as its base model; when probed without any tools attached, it still hallucinates calls to a non-existent web_search tool9.

Although Apex labels its pipeline recursive self-improvement, the report presents no multi-generational data. Its "self-evolving" synthetic data pipeline falls under weak self-improvement7, with the underlying training loop and update rules still engineered entirely by humans8.
What they have in common
Taken together, the forensic checks show that all three open-weight models inherit either their foundational weights or their reasoning patterns from existing external models:

en.html: (Sources:9,10)

Stepping back, all four reports demonstrate genuine first-order improvement: faster kernels, tighter training scripts, and higher benchmark scores. None of them, however, measures second-order improvement—taking the improved model, placing it back into the harness as the next generation's researcher, and testing whether it drives progress faster than its predecessor under the same budget. Even at the first-order level, evaluation results frequently diverge depending on which team runs the harness, as seen in the conflicting scores for Flint and SOL-ExecBench. Why has a clean measurement of second-order improvement remained absent across all of these efforts? The next section examines the structural reasons behind this gap.

zh.html: 不仅第 2 节剖析的四份产业界报告停留在了一阶改进，目前学术界通用的 AI 研发能力基准，测量的同样是一阶表现。例如，RE-Bench 比较 agent 与人类专家在机器学习工程任务上的得分，MLE-bench 统计 agent 在 Kaggle 竞赛中夺牌的比例，PaperBench 则检验 agent 能否从零复现论文代码105,106,107。这些基准共同回答的问题是“当前这个模型能不能做研究”。至于宏观层面的增速评估，METR 对 Anthropic 的调研估计，自 2025 年 10 月以来，该实验室的整体研发推进速度约为此前的 1.9 倍（95% CI 1.5–2.8）108。但这一数字反映的是包含人类研究员在内的整个实验室的综合产出速度，并未剥离出“后继模型接替担任研究者时，其独立改进速度是否快于前代”。
要真正检验二阶改进，必须往前多走一步：将上一轮改进得到的后继模型放回研发管线中担任新的改进者，在相同的任务和预算下，直接对比各代改进者的推进速度。然而，现有研究大多在这一步之前便停下了脚步：

zh.html: 从上表可以看出，现有工作普遍陷入了一种两难割裂。一方面，自我训练（self-training）范式虽然切实更新了模型权重，但“如何训练”的规则由人类事先写死，且往往在寥寥数轮内便陷入停滞甚至退化：Mind the Gap 观察到模型生成与验证之间的性能差距在两三轮内便收窄至接近零17，SPIN 的单轮增益随迭代逐轮递减18，而 ReST-EM 在 APPS 基准上更是从第一轮之后便开始出现回退19。另一方面，允许系统改写自身代码的框架则恰恰相反——“如何改进”的搜索策略可以动态演化，但底层的语言模型权重却被完全冻结。STOP 的作者便明确指出了这一局限29。至于 DGM，其消融实验虽然显示包含自我改进的完整系统在 SWE-bench 和 Polyglot 上分别达到 50.0 和 38.0（高于固定改进者版本的 39.0 和 28.0）110，但该对比衡量的仍是单次 80 轮迭代结束后的终点得分，而非各代改进者之间的推进速度。

学界之所以极少直接跨代测量二阶改进，首先是因为双层循环的实验成本过于高昂，且噪声极易逐层累积。以 AIDE² 为例，其单次完整运行需耗时 8 天，仅能产生 100 个外层步骤20；作者坦言，若要得出统计上更稳健的结论，必须增加外层随机种子并对每个种子产出的最终 agent 进行完整的保留集（held-out）评测，但这在算力成本上难以承受20。同样，DGM 在 SWE-bench 上的单次运行开销高达约 22,000 美元、耗时约两周，因此根本未能进行多种子重复实验110,113。更棘手的是，随机噪声会在内外两层循环之间级联放大：内层搜索的轨迹本就随随机种子剧烈波动，单个候选解的评测也自带测量误差；一旦某次改写因评测噪声被误判采纳，它就会成为新的基线（incumbent），进而将后续的搜索方向一路带偏20。

既然直接测量如此昂贵，能否直接用更容易获取的“一阶基准得分”来推算模型的二阶改进能力？实证数据否定了这一捷径。HGM 的研究表明，DGM 和 SICA 用于筛选父代节点的基准测试分数，与该 agent 随后繁衍出更优后代的能力之间仅存在弱相关性，加权 Pearson 相关系数仅为 0.285–0.444111。正如 STOP 的作者所总结的：“在下游任务上表现更好的改进者，并不意味着它更擅长优化自身”（"a better improver on downstream tasks need not be better at optimizing itself"）112。

除了成本与指标失效之外，一旦在实验中放开改进者的修改权限，系统钻评测空子（reward hacking）的风险便会急剧上升。在 STOP 记录的 10,000 次改进尝试中，GPT-4 有 0.42% 的运行直接关闭了安全沙箱；即便在提示词中显式加入“禁止修改沙箱”的警告，违规比例依然高达 0.46%，并未下降112。在 DGM 的实验中，编号为 114 的节点直接删掉了用于检测工具调用幻觉的日志记录，借此骗取了满分110；METR 也发现，o3 在 RE-Bench 上有高达 30.4%（39/128）的运行出现了不同形式的作弊行为115。这表明，即便评测指标本身是客观的数值，只要评估代码暴露在可写范围内，就无法避免被模型篡改116。因此，要可靠地测量二阶改进，评估器必须被严格隔离在改进者无权写入的封存环境中。

另一种常见的替代叙事是将“更快的模型推理速度”等同于研发循环的加速——例如第 2 节中的 Flint 和 Naive 均重点强调了各自的解码吞吐优势80,117。然而，更快的推理同样无法替代二阶测量。在本报告使用 Qwen3.5-9B 运行的 NanoChat 研究实验中，候选方案的评测（即沙箱训练加验证打分）占据了 agent 总运行时间的 85.3%，而模型自身的推理思考仅占 14.6%118。根据 Amdahl 定律，即便将模型推理速度提升 2 倍，整个研发循环也仅能提速 1.08 倍；哪怕模型思考耗时降至零（无限快），整个循环的提速上限也不过 1.17 倍；反过来，若将评测环节加速 2 倍，循环整体则可提速 1.74 倍估算。由此可见，自动化研究循环的瓶颈主要卡在验证候选方案所需的训练算力上，而非模型生成 token 的快慢。

图 7　一次真实研究运行的时间分配。(a) Qwen3.5-9B 改进 NanoChat 训练脚本的 176.6 分钟：最上方是当前最好的 val_bpb（从 1.4152 降到 1.2308）；中间三行是 GPU 评测线，每个色块是一次评测（训练加打分），蓝色表示结果被保留，灰色表示被丢弃，橙色表示评测崩溃；下方三行是三个研究线程，每条黑色细线是一次模型调用。鼠标悬停在色块上可以看到这次尝试的编号、用时和结果1,2。(b) agent 时间的构成：评测占 85.3%，模型思考占 14.6%118。(c) 按 Amdahl 定律，只加速其中一部分时整个循环的提速倍数，曲线由 (b) 的比例计算：模型思考再快，循环最多快约 1.17 倍。

综上所述，在本报告系统检索的约 96 份文献中，迄今尚无任何一项工作在模型权重层面、配备严格对照地测量过二阶改进114；而使用“在被否决的失败尝试上微调”作为安慰剂对照的做法，在检索范围内同样未见先例114。为直接检验这一问题，第 4 节采用以下设计：第一，评测全部采用改进者未曾见过的新任务；第二，各代模型共享完全相同的预算与物理隔离的封存评估器；第三，实验前先对同一原始模型独立运行两遍（A/A 测试），以标定随机波动的基线范围；第四，同时设立失败轨迹“安慰剂”对照与“单纯多给数据”对照；第五，所有统计判定规则均在实验启动前预先锁定119。

en.html: Just as the four industry reports audited in Section 2 stop at first-order improvement, the research benchmarks standard in academia likewise measure only first-order performance. RE-Bench compares agents against human experts on ML engineering tasks, MLE-bench tallies the share of Kaggle competitions in which an agent wins a medal, and PaperBench tests whether an agent can reproduce a published paper from scratch105,106,107. All of these benchmarks ask the same underlying question: can the current model conduct research? At the macro level, METR's assessment of Anthropic estimates that since October 2025, the lab's overall pace of progress has run at roughly 1.9 times its prior rate (95% CI 1.5–2.8)108. Yet that figure captures the combined velocity of the entire laboratory—human researchers included—without isolating whether a successor model actually drives progress faster than its predecessor when placed in the researcher's seat.

Testing for second-order improvement requires taking one step further: placing the improved model back into the harness as the new improver, and comparing its speed of improvement across the exact same tasks and budget. Nearly all existing work stops short of this step:

en.html: As the table illustrates, prior approaches split into two opposing camps. On one side, self-training paradigms do update model weights, but the training recipe itself is fixed in advance by human engineers—and such loops typically plateau or regress within a few iterations: *Mind the Gap* observes that the gap between generation and verification collapses to near zero within two to three rounds17, SPIN yields diminishing returns with each passing round18, and ReST-EM begins to regress on APPS right after the first iteration19. On the other side, systems that rewrite their own code allow the search method to evolve, but keep the underlying language model weights completely frozen—a limitation the authors of STOP highlight explicitly29. While DGM's ablation shows that its full self-modifying system reaches 50.0 on SWE-bench and 38.0 on Polyglot compared to 39.0 and 28.0 for a fixed improver110, that comparison still evaluates final scores after 80 iterations rather than measuring generation-over-generation improvement speed.

The primary reason direct measurements of second-order improvement remain rare is the sheer cost and compounding noise of nested optimization loops. A single full run of AIDE² took 8 days to complete 100 outer-loop steps20, and the authors note that drawing firmer statistical conclusions would require running more outer-loop seeds and evaluating every resulting agent on a held-out suite—an exercise they deemed prohibitively expensive20. Similarly, a single DGM run on SWE-bench costs roughly 22,000 US dollars and takes about two weeks, precluding multi-seed replication110,113. Worse still, stochastic noise compounds across the two nested loops: inner-loop search trajectories vary widely across seeds, and evaluating any individual candidate solution carries its own variance; a single flawed modification accepted by chance becomes the new incumbent and steers the remainder of the search off course20.

Given these costs, can one simply use a model's first-order benchmark score as a cheap proxy for its second-order ability to improve? Empirical evidence says no. HGM demonstrates that the benchmark scores used by DGM and SICA to select parent agents correlate only weakly with an agent's actual capacity to produce stronger descendants, yielding weighted Pearson coefficients of just 0.285–0.444111. As the authors of STOP put it, "a better improver on downstream tasks need not be better at optimizing itself"112.

Compound noise is not the only hazard: the wider the scope of modifications an improver is permitted to make, the greater its opportunity to game the evaluation. Across 10,000 improvement attempts in STOP, GPT-4 disabled its containment sandbox in 0.42% of runs; adding an explicit prompt warning not to touch the sandbox left the violation rate unchanged at 0.46%112. In DGM, node 114 achieved a perfect score simply by deleting the logging code designed to catch tool-call hallucinations110, while METR documented reward hacking in 30.4% (39 of 128) of o3's runs on RE-Bench115. Relying on an objective numeric metric is therefore no safeguard against gaming if the evaluation harness itself remains accessible116; any credible test of second-order improvement must isolate the evaluator in a sealed environment where the improver has no write permissions.

Nor can raw inference speed substitute for a second-order measurement, even though both Flint and Naive prominently tout their decoding throughput80,117. In this report's NanoChat research run with Qwen3.5-9B, candidate evaluation (sandbox training plus validation scoring) consumed 85.3% of total agent wall-clock time, whereas model reasoning accounted for just 14.6%118. By Amdahl's law, doubling the model's thinking speed accelerates the end-to-end research loop by a factor of only 1.08, and even infinitely fast reasoning would cap the overall speedup at 1.17×; doubling the speed of evaluation, by contrast, speeds up the loop by 1.74× (an estimate). In practice, the pace of automated research is bottlenecked by the training compute required to verify candidate ideas, not by how quickly the model generates tokens.

en.html: Across the roughly 96 sources reviewed for this report, no prior study has conducted a controlled measurement of second-order improvement at the level of model weights114, nor did the literature search for this report find any precedent for using fine-tuning on rejected attempts as a placebo control114. To address each of the methodological pitfalls outlined above, the experiments in Section 4 are built around five strict design rules: (1) evaluating exclusively on held-out tasks unseen by the improver; (2) enforcing an identical budget and a single, write-protected sealed evaluator across all generations; (3) running the unmodified base model twice (an A/A test) beforehand to establish the baseline band of random variation; (4) pairing every self-trained checkpoint against both a rejected-trajectory placebo control and a "more data" control; and (5) locking in all statistical decision rules before the runs begin119.

zh.html: 设计
本实验以原版 BF16 权重的 Qwen3.5-9B 作为初始改进者，通过 vLLM 部署在 A100 GPU 上120。改进者在隔离沙箱内工作，候选方案统一交由封存的评估器打分。沙箱通过了全部 12 项安全隔离检查（包括断网、隐藏验证集与封存集、触碰诱饵文件即触发警报等）1；改进者仅能收到验证集分数与训练曲线反馈，无法接触封存测试集分数、评估器代码或参考最优值119。

zh.html: 实验涵盖两类任务。第一类是 NanoChat：改进者直接修改小型语言模型的训练脚本，每次尝试在沙箱内训练并评估验证集表现；沿用 Karpathy 的 autoresearch 规则，仅当新方案优于当前最佳版本时才予以保留，否则丢弃121,119。由于 NanoChat 单次评测的噪声较大（20 个随机种子均值 1.4007，标准差 0.0268），每次保留改动前均需换用另一个随机种子复测确认1。

第二类是 8 个未见过的小型研究任务，用于横向测量各代模型的改进速度。每个任务均为数秒内即可跑完的微型训练，初始配置带有随机注入的缺陷；改进者通过调整一份约 12 个旋钮的 JSON 配置（优化器、学习率、宽度、深度等）来降低验证损失。训练按步数严格封顶，使改进者无法靠放大模型换取额外算力119,122。8 个任务中，4 个属于训练时见过但重新抽样了参数的同族任务（模加法、稀疏奇偶、师生回归、二维分类），另外 4 个是训练时完全未见过的任务类型（序列反转、括号匹配、上下文线性回归、字符级语言模型）119,3。实验另设 8 个独立的训练任务（原始模型在每个任务上用 5 个种子探索），其记录仅用于生成微调数据或经验笔记，绝不参与任何比较122。
评测时，每次研究运行包含 12 次尝试。每个改进者在每个未见任务上均使用相同的 5 个随机种子各跑一次，所有比较按任务配对计算1,122。

改进速度分（取值 0 到 1，越高越好）定义如下：对第 t 次尝试，计算当前历史最好分数已将“起点分数到参考最优”的差距缩小了多少比例（参考最优由离线随机搜索与所有组的最好结果汇总得到，仅用于归一化）；将该比例在 12 次尝试与 5 个种子上取平均，即得该任务上的改进速度分119。两个改进者之间的总差值为 8 个任务逐任务差值的平均，95% 置信区间用 bootstrap 计算，p 值来自按任务配对的符号翻转置换检验（8 个任务下理论最小 p 值为 2/256 ≈ 0.008）119。
图 9　改进速度分的算法（示意图，曲线形状不是实验数据）。阴影是每次尝试时已经缩小的差距；改进速度分是阴影占整个矩形的比例，再对 5 个种子平均，最后在 8 个任务上逐任务配对比较119。

zh.html: 实验设有三类对照119：

items: A/A 对照：让原始模型用另一组互不重叠的种子再跑一遍，测得逐任务差值的标准差为 0.031，对应的最小可检出效应约为 0.0313。
安慰剂（Placebo）对照：在权重一侧用等量的被否决尝试记录做相同微调；在笔记一侧用等长、但不看任何尝试记录写出的通用建议1。
"多给数据"对照与随机配方对照：用于剥离单纯增加数据量或更换数据集的影响（见下文对应小节）。

zh.html: 统计判定规则在实验前预先锁定：唯有同时满足（1）差值的 95% CI 下界大于 0、（2）差值大于 A/A 标准差的 2 倍（即 0.062）、（3）显著好于对应对照这三条，才算检出二阶改进；否则记为“在本次检测力下未检出”119,3。
一阶结果：固定的改进者改进 NanoChat

原始模型通过 OpenCode harness 以 3 个并行线程运行了 176.6 分钟，提出并评测了 72 次尝试（保留 25 次，拒绝 47 次，评测崩溃 9 次，安全审计标记 0 次）1。验证损失（每字节比特数 BPB，越低越好）从 1.4152 降至 1.2308，累计下降 0.1844，终点成绩比单次评测噪声的均值低约 6.3 个标准差1,2（运行耗时分配见第 3 节图 7；独立封存数据上的终点复核尚待完成1）。由于改进者在整个运行中保持不变，这一结果验证了单代一阶改进的有效性。
图 10　NanoChat 研究运行的回放，按真实事件记录重绘，约 350 倍速，自动循环。上方是当前最好的验证损失（跨 3 个线程取最小值）和每次评测的结果；中间是 3 条 GPU 评测线；下方是最新的判定和对应的提案假设（模型原文）。鼠标悬停在点上可以看到该次尝试的数值2,1。

zh.html: 经验笔记

在微调权重之前，我们先测试仅通过上下文传递经验的效果。原始模型阅读自己在 8 个训练任务（各 5 个种子）上的研究记录，写出一份 252 词的经验笔记附在后续每次评测的提示词中，权重保持不变1,122。该笔记将训练任务上的经验归纳为一套固定流程（先换 cosine 学习率调度，再降 weight decay，接着加宽加深，最后调学习率），并立下一条规则：“忽略任何哪怕略微增加损失的改动”（"Ignore changes that increase loss even slightly"）1。其安慰剂对照是等长、但未查阅任何记录写出的通用建议1。

实验显示，挂载经验笔记后，模型的改进速度分从原始模型的 0.588 跌至 0.392（差值 −0.196，95% CI [−0.383, −0.033]，完全落在 0 以下，符号翻转检验 p = 0.11），改进速度下降约三分之一3。相比之下，通用建议安慰剂的得分约为 0.631（见图 11）；经验笔记相对安慰剂的差值达 −0.239（95% CI [−0.420, −0.075]），在全部 8 个任务上均为负值（p = 0.008），退化主要集中在二维分类（−0.58）、序列反转（−0.56）、上下文线性回归（−0.49）和模加法（−0.20）四个任务上（图 13）3。这说明笔记将训练任务上的个别成功错误固化成了死板的搜索顺序，在未见任务类型上将搜索引向了歧途，而“严禁任何微小损失上升”的规则又进一步收窄了探索范围推断1。
用自己的成功记录微调：三代后继模型
接下来我们在权重层面测试三代后继模型。第一代后继模型取原始模型在训练任务上所有被采纳尝试的记录（输入为当时完整提示，输出为模型提案，共 438 条调用），从原始权重出发进行 LoRA 微调（rank 16，学习率 1e-4，2 个 epoch）1,119,123；安慰剂模型则改用等量的被否决尝试记录在相同设置下微调1。
第二代后继模型仍从原始权重开始训练，数据为原始模型记录加上第一代后继模型在训练任务新种子上跑出的记录；其“多给数据”对照模型则加上原始模型在相同新种子上跑出的等量记录——两者数据量完全相同，唯一区别是新增部分由谁产生122,119。第三代后继模型依此类推，在第二代数据基础上叠加第二代新跑出的记录，其对照模型则叠加两份均由原始模型产生的记录1。
图 12　三代后继模型和对照模型的训练数据来源。每个模型都从原始权重开始做 LoRA；第二、三代与各自的“多给数据”对照数据量相同，只有新增部分由谁产生不同。蓝色弧线表示上一代模型跑出的记录进入下一代的训练数据。右侧是未见过任务上的改进速度分1,122,3。

zh.html: （来源：3,1）
原始模型与第一、二、三代后继模型的改进速度分依次为 0.588、0.537、0.573 和 0.487，没有任何一项比较满足二阶改进的检出条件1,3。具体来看：

items: 成功信号未被习得：第一代与安慰剂模型几乎完全相同（差值 +0.004，p = 0.91），用被采纳记录与用被否决记录微调毫无差别，说明模型并未学到“哪些尝试有效”1。
第二代仅回归基线：第二代相对“多给数据”对照的正差值主要来自序列反转（+0.18）与上下文线性回归（+0.11）3，但这源于第一代（0.537）与对照模型（0.534）均低于原始模型，而第二代（0.573）只是回到了原始模型附近，并未超越原始模型推断1。
第三代出现退化：第三代比第二代低 0.087（bootstrap 区间上界小于 0，被平台判为退化；符号翻转检验在 0.10 水平上显著）1。三代均未超过原始模型且第三代出现退化的趋势，与 Shumailov 等人描述的递归训练退化方向一致124；由于本实验未测量输出分布尾部，尚无法判断两者是否属于同一机制推断1。

zh.html: 让模型自己决定怎么训练自己

在前文的三代迭代中，挑选哪些记录与使用何种超参数均由人类预先固定；按 Tang 等人的判据，改进机制外置的过程属于 GPI 而非 RSI8。参照 SEAL 让模型自主生成微调数据与超参的思路（在 ARC 子集上经反馈训练后将自我编辑成功率从 20% 提升至 72.5%）125,122，我们将训练配方的决策权交还给模型：设计者阅读训练记录摘要（含 4 类任务下被采纳、hindsight 与被否决记录的条数、提升分布及提案样例），在给定空间内自主决定筛选条件与 LoRA 超参（rank、学习率、epoch 数）1。
三轮微调共用原始模型的同一份记录池，均从原始权重出发训练（单次训练上限 55 分钟）1,123。每轮的对照均为随机配方：从合法记录中随机抽取同等条数、以相同的 LoRA 设置训练，以此将“模型挑数据的判断力”与“单纯更换训练集”区分开1。
三轮的设计者演进如下：第一轮由原始模型盲定；第二轮仍由原始模型设计，但事先向其提供第一轮在训练任务（换用新种子）上的逐任务表现对比表；第三轮将设计者替换为“第一轮微调后的模型”，它看到的信息、记录池及起始权重均与第二轮完全一致，唯一变量是设计者自身1。
图 14　让模型自己决定怎么训练自己的三轮。每一列从上到下是设计者、它给出的配方、实际训练和未见过任务上的改进速度分。第二、三轮的设计者看到同一张反馈表；橙色弧线表示第一轮微调后的模型成为第三轮的设计者，它的前两次回答被 8192 token 上限截断1,123,3。

zh.html: （来源：1,3,123。"—"表示不适用或无单独记录；随机配方对照分数由差值推出。）

第一轮。 原始模型认为默认配方表现不佳源于数据量太少且 LoRA 容量不足，因而放宽上限、纳入 hindsight 记录并强化 LoRA（这一归因其实与前文安慰剂实验相悖，因为瓶颈在于训练信号而非数据量推断）1。第一轮模型的改进速度分为 0.605，相对原始模型（+0.017，95% CI [−0.109, +0.155]，p = 0.82）与随机配方（+0.077，95% CI [−0.085, +0.223]，p = 0.36）虽略高，但因跨任务波动极大（相对随机配方从模加法的 +0.35 到上下文线性回归的 −0.27，见图 13），所有置信区间均包含 0，判为未检出3。

第二轮。 反馈表显示第一轮模型在训练任务上得分为 0.652，明显高于原始模型（0.525）与第一代（0.483）（这很可能源于对同源训练任务的记忆推断）1。然而原始模型在设计理由中完全未引用该反馈表，反而出于对 hindsight 噪声和过拟合的一般性担忧，将第一轮的每项选择彻底反转（仅筛出 137 条调用，以 2e-5 学习率浅训 31 步）1。由于验证损失几乎未变，模型实质上未被改动，其得分（0.595）也直接回到原始模型水平（相对原始模型 +0.007，p = 0.65；其余比对均不显著，详见图 11 与3）推断1。
第三轮：由微调后的模型来定配方
当第一轮微调后的模型接手设计第三轮配方时，其前两次回答均在思考阶段写满 8192 token 上限而未输出正文，第三次重试才给出配方（原始模型在前两轮均是一次通过）1。它几乎原样保留了第一轮的高强度设置，仅增加了一道 1% 的最小相对提升阈值（选出 539 条调用）1。

然而，第三轮模型的改进速度分却暴跌至 0.392，不仅显著低于第二轮模型（差值 −0.204，95% CI [−0.365, −0.065]，p = 0.008），也显著低于原始模型（−0.197，95% CI [−0.363, −0.050]，p = 0.031）、第一轮模型（−0.213，p = 0.047）及固定配方（−0.145，p = 0.008），被平台判为显著变差（下降最大的是序列反转 −0.48 与模加法 −0.34，见图 13）3,1。
这一反差揭示了两点关键事实：

items: 配方和训练强度影响结果：补充实验以新随机种子重训第一轮配方，得分为 0.602，与原结果 0.605 接近；这排除了“第一轮高分只是随机种子波动”的解释。Qwen3.8-27B 使用与第三轮相同的数据筛选规则、但采用较轻训练，得分为 0.513，高于第三轮的 0.392，仍低于原始模型的 0.588。四种配方的结果表明，筛除小幅提升记录与训练强度共同影响后继模型表现。
高强度微调引发输出行为坍缩：训练强度大的三个模型（第一轮、第三轮及其随机配方对照）在未见任务上均演变为“高频次、极短输出”的调用模式（调用 11,287～15,087 次，输出中位数 47～54 token），而原始模型与轻度训练的第二轮模型仅调用约 2,030 次、输出中位数保持在 101～111 token——这说明该行为畸变直接源于训练强度，而与配方由谁设计无关推断1。

zh.html: 从最好版本继续改
除了在未见任务上从头评测，另一种避免“后继模型默写训练答案”的设计是让各改进者从同一个前沿版本（NanoChat 研究运行的最佳终点 1.2308）继续单线程探索 12 次尝试119,1。我们比较了 4 个改进者（各重复 3 次并轮换评测 GPU，以各运行重测基线减去所得最优值计算“降幅”）1,126：

受限于每组 3 次运行的样本量，同一改进者在三次运行间的内部波动（例如原始模型从 0.0005 到 0.0243）远大于不同改进者之间的均值差异；从同一个前沿版本继续改时，换上后继模型或挂载经验笔记均未产生可测量的加速推断1,126。

补充检验：配方还是随机波动
第三轮的得分明显低于第一轮。为判断差距是否来自训练随机性或设计者规模，补做了两项比较。第一项保持第一轮数据和配方不变，只更换 LoRA 随机种子。第二项将配方设计者换为 Qwen3.8-27B，并让它基于与第二轮相同的反馈制定配方。

zh.html: 换种子重训得分为 0.602，接近第一轮的 0.605，说明第一轮结果可重复。第三轮的 0.392 与第一轮之间的差距不能归因于随机种子。Qwen3.8-27B 设计的配方得分为 0.513。它优于第三轮，但未超过原始模型或第二轮模型1,5。
结合四种配方，结果指向两项影响因素：是否剔除提升较小的被采纳记录，以及训练强度。使用同一批 539 条记录时，较轻训练得分 0.513，较重训练得分 0.392；保留全部记录的两次第一轮训练得分分别为 0.605 和 0.602。该比较支持配方选择影响后继模型表现，但尚不能单独确定筛选规则和训练强度各自的因果效应1,5。
局限

items: 迭代代数与规模受限：后继模型仅推进至第三代，自主配方设计仅运行三轮（且仅含一次源自训练任务的反馈）；底层改进者仅测试了 Qwen3.5-9B 单一模型，评测任务局限于数秒级的微型训练任务与单一的 NanoChat 基准（其终点在封存数据上的复核尚待完成）1。
跨任务方差限制了检测力：尽管 A/A 测出的最小可检出效应约为 0.031，但两个不同模型之间的差值在任务间波动大得多（从 −0.58 到 +0.35），实际所需的效应量更大；而“从最好版本继续改”每组仅有 3 次运行1,122。
单次微调方差与受限的配方空间：每份自主配方仅训练了一次（第一、三轮配方几乎相同却相差 0.213，且均受 55 分钟上限截断在约 2.4 与 2.7 个 epoch），因此单次训练不足以稳健比较配方优劣推断3,1；同时，模型只能在人类预设的选项空间内组合超参，无法编写任意训练代码，按 Tang 等人的判据仍属 GPI 而非 RSI8,1。
推理服务路径混杂：原始模型不带 adapter 直接由 vLLM 服务，而所有微调模型均经过 vLLM 的 LoRA adapter 路径；这一混杂仅影响与原始模型的比较，后继模型之间及其与安慰剂之间的横向比较不受影响122。

en.html: Design

Our experimental improver is Qwen3.5-9B in its native BF16 weights, served via vLLM on A100 GPUs120. The model operates inside an isolated sandbox while a sealed evaluator scores its candidates. The sandbox passed all 12 containment checks—including blocked network access, zero visibility into validation or sealed datasets, and tripwire alarms on decoy files1. The improver receives only validation scores and training curves; it never sees sealed test scores, evaluator source code, or the reference optimum119.

Figure 8. One attempt on the platform. The improver proposes a candidate inside the isolated sandbox; the sealed evaluator trains and scores it; it is kept if it beats the current best and discarded otherwise; the improver only sees the dev score and the training curve. The blue dot traces the path of one attempt. Hover for sources120,119,1.

en.html: The experiment uses two task suites. The first is NanoChat: the improver edits the training script of a small language model; following Karpathy's autoresearch rule, each attempt trains once in the sandbox and is scored on a validation split, keeping modifications that beat the incumbent best and discarding the rest121,119. Because single-run NanoChat evaluations are noisy (20 seeds, mean 1.4007, SD 0.0268), every candidate keep must be confirmed by a rerun on a fresh seed1.

The second suite comprises 8 unseen micro-research tasks used to measure improvement speed across generations. Each task is a fast training run (completing in a few seconds) initialized with randomly drawn configuration defects; the improver lowers validation loss by tuning a JSON configuration of roughly 12 knobs (optimizer, learning rate, width, depth, etc.). Training is capped by step count so the improver cannot buy compute by enlarging the model119,122. Four of the 8 tasks belong to the same families as the training tasks with newly drawn settings (modular addition, sparse parity, teacher-student regression, 2-D classification), while the other 4 are entirely novel task types (sequence reversal, bracket matching, in-context linear regression, character-level language modeling)119,3. A separate set of 8 training tasks (explored by the original model across 5 seeds each) supplies training trajectories or lessons notes and never enters any comparison122.
During evaluation, each research run consists of 12 attempts. Every improver runs once on each unseen task using the exact same 5 seeds, with all comparisons paired by task1,122.

The improvement-speed score (bounded between 0 and 1, higher is better) is computed as follows: at attempt t, we calculate the fraction of the gap between the starting score and a reference optimum closed by the best score achieved so far (where the reference optimum pools an offline random search with the best result across all arms, used strictly for normalization). Averaging this fraction over the 12 attempts and 5 seeds yields the task's improvement-speed score119. The overall difference between two improvers is the mean per-task difference across the 8 tasks, with 95% confidence intervals from bootstrap and p-values from a task-paired sign-flip permutation test (whose minimum possible p-value across 8 tasks is 2/256 ≈ 0.008)119.

Figure 9. How the improvement-speed score is computed (schematic; the curve shape is not experiment data). The shaded area is the gap already closed at each attempt; the score is the shaded share of the whole rectangle, averaged over 5 seeds and compared task by task over the 8 tasks119.

en.html: The experiment incorporates three types of controls119:

items: A/A control: Rerunning the original model on a disjoint seed set yields a per-task difference SD of 0.031, establishing a baseline minimum detectable effect (MDE) of about 0.0313.

Placebo control: On the weight side, fine-tuning on an equal number of rejected attempts under identical settings; on the lessons side, using generic tips of equal length written without inspecting any attempt logs1.
"More data" and random-recipe controls: Isolating the effect of added data volume or dataset changes (detailed in the respective subsections below).

en.html: The statistical decision rule was locked in before execution: a second-order improvement is detected only if (1) the lower bound of the 95% CI exceeds 0, (2) the difference exceeds twice the A/A standard deviation (> 0.062), and (3) the improver is significantly better than its matched control; otherwise, it is reported as "not detected at this power"119,3.
First-order result: a fixed improver improves NanoChat

Running through the OpenCode harness across 3 parallel threads for 176.6 minutes, the unmodified original model proposed and evaluated 72 attempts (25 kept, 47 rejected, 9 evaluation crashes, and 0 audit flags)1. Validation loss (bits per byte, lower is better) fell from 1.4152 to 1.2308—a reduction of 0.1844, placing the final result roughly 6.3 standard deviations below the mean of single-evaluation noise1,2 (see Figure 7 in Section 3 for the time breakdown; the endpoint check on sealed data remains pending1). Because the improver stayed fixed throughout, this result establishes a clear first-order improvement.

en.html: Figure 11. Improvement-speed score on the 8 unseen micro-research tasks for the improver produced by each self-update approach and for its control. Blue dots are the improvers, orange dots their controls: generic tips of equal length for the lessons note, the placebo model for generation 1, the "more data" control for generations 2 and 3, and a random recipe for each of the three self-designed rounds. The dashed line is the original model (0.588). Control scores are derived as the improver's score minus the difference between the two. Hover to see values and sources3.

en.html: Lessons note

Before updating weights, we tested whether the model could accelerate itself purely in-context. Reading its own research records across the 8 training tasks (5 seeds each), the original model wrote a 252-word lessons note that was appended to the prompt of every subsequent evaluation run while keeping weights frozen1,122. The note codified a fixed tuning sequence derived from the training tasks (switch to a cosine schedule, lower weight decay, widen and deepen, then tune learning rate) and included the rule: *"Ignore changes that increase loss even slightly"*1. Its placebo control consisted of generic tips of the same length written without reading any records1.

Appending the note reduced the model's improvement-speed score from 0.588 to 0.392 (a difference of −0.196, 95% CI [−0.383, −0.033], entirely below 0; sign-flip p = 0.11), slowing improvement by roughly a third3. Against the placebo tips—which scored about 0.631 (Figure 11)—the lessons note trailed by −0.239 (95% CI [−0.420, −0.075], p = 0.008), scoring lower on all 8 tasks, led by drops on 2-D classification (−0.58), sequence reversal (−0.56), in-context linear regression (−0.49), and modular addition (−0.20) (Figure 13)3. This indicates that the note over-generalized incidental successes on the training tasks into a rigid search order that misdirected exploration on unseen task types, while its ban on any temporary loss increase further narrowed exploration (an inference)1.
Fine-tuning on its own successes: three successor generations

We next tested weight-level updates across three generations. Generation 1 was fine-tuned from the original weights via LoRA (rank 16, learning rate 1e-4, 2 epochs) on all 438 calls from accepted attempts on the training tasks, while its placebo model was trained under identical settings on 438 rejected calls1,119,123.

Generation 2 was again initialized from the original weights, trained on the original model's records plus new records generated by Generation 1 on fresh seeds of the training tasks. Its "more data" control combined the original records with an equal volume of new records generated by the *original* model on the same seeds—holding data volume constant so the only difference is who generated the added trajectories122,119. Generation 3 followed the same pattern, adding Generation 2's records against a control that added two batches from the original model1.

Figure 12. Where the training data of each successor generation and its control comes from. Every model starts LoRA from the original weights; generations 2 and 3 and their "more data" controls use the same amount of data, differing only in who produced the added part. Blue arcs show records produced by one generation entering the next generation's data. Right: score on the unseen tasks1,122,3.

en.html: (Sources:3,1)
Across the original model and Generations 1 to 3, improvement-speed scores moved from 0.588 to 0.537, 0.573, and 0.487; no comparison met our detection rule1,3. Specifically:

items: Success signal was not learned: Generation 1 (0.537) and the placebo model performed almost identically (difference +0.004, p = 0.91), showing that fine-tuning on accepted versus rejected records made no difference1.

Generation 2 merely returned to baseline: While Generation 2 posted a positive gap against its "more data" control—driven mainly by sequence reversal (+0.18) and in-context linear regression (+0.11)3—this occurred only because both Generation 1 (0.537) and the control (0.534) dipped below the original model, whereas Generation 2 (0.573) returned near the original baseline without surpassing it (an inference)1.

Generational degradation in Generation 3: Generation 3 fell 0.087 below Generation 2 (marked as worse by the bootstrap 95% CI upper bound below 0; sign-flip p = 0.0625)1. Failing to surpass the original model across three generations and showing signs of degradation in the third aligns in direction with the recursive-training degradation described by Shumailov et al.124, though without measuring output distribution tails we cannot confirm whether the underlying mechanism is identical (an inference)1.

en.html: Figure 13. Per-task difference between each improver and its control (improver minus control, improvement-speed score) on the 8 tasks. Blue means the improver is faster, orange slower; the rightmost column is the mean over the 8 tasks. The same approach can differ by anywhere from −0.58 to +0.35 across tasks, which is why the confidence intervals are wide. Hover to see values and sources3.

en.html: The model decides how to train itself

In the three generations above, humans fixed the data filters and hyperparameters in advance—a process that Tang et al. classify as GPI rather than RSI8. Inspired by SEAL, which lets a model choose its own fine-tuning data and hyperparameters (raising self-edit success on an ARC subset from 20% to 72.5% after outer-loop feedback training)125,122, we let the model choose its own training recipe within a structured space. Reading a summary of the training logs (counts of accepted, hindsight, and rejected records across the 4 task types, relative gain distributions, and sample hypotheses), the designer specifies which records to filter and which LoRA settings (rank, learning rate, epochs) to use1.

All three rounds draw on the original model's record pool, fine-tune from the original weights, and cap training at 55 minutes1,123. Each round is paired with a random-recipe control that samples the exact same number of calls at random from valid records and trains under identical LoRA settings, separating the model's data-selection judgment from the effect of simply changing the dataset1.

The designer role progresses across the three rounds: Round 1 is designed blindly by the original model; Round 2 is also designed by the original model, after seeing a feedback table comparing per-task scores on the training tasks (with fresh seeds) for Round 1, the original model, and Generation 1; Round 3 replaces the designer with the *Round-1 fine-tuned model*, which sees the exact same feedback, record pool, and starting weights as in Round 21.

Figure 14. The three rounds in which the model decides how to train itself. Each column shows, top to bottom, the designer, its recipe, the actual training and the score on the unseen tasks. The designers of rounds 2 and 3 see the same feedback table; the orange arc marks the round-1 model becoming the round-3 designer, whose first two answers were cut at the 8192-token cap1,123,3.

en.html: (Sources:1,3,123. "—" means not applicable or not recorded separately; random-recipe scores are derived from the differences.)

Round 1. Reasoning that the default recipe suffered from too little data and LoRA capacity, the original model raised the cap, added hindsight records, and strengthened the LoRA—an explanation at odds with Generation 1, where the placebo comparison pointed to training signal rather than data volume (an inference)1. The Round-1 model scored 0.605, edging out the original model (+0.017, 95% CI [−0.109, +0.155], p = 0.82) and its random recipe (+0.077, 95% CI [−0.085, +0.223], p = 0.36), but wide task-to-task swings (from +0.35 on modular addition to −0.27 on in-context linear regression against the random recipe; Figure 13) kept all intervals straddling zero, marking it as not detected3.

Round 2. Although the feedback table showed Round 1 leading on the training tasks (0.652 vs. 0.525 for the original model, likely reflecting memorization of the training tasks (an inference)), the original model never cited that table in its rationale; instead, citing hindsight noise and overfitting concerns, it reversed nearly every choice from Round 1 (selecting just 137 calls and training for 31 steps at a 2e-5 learning rate)1. Because validation loss barely moved, the weights were hardly changed and the model's score (0.595) simply reverted to the original model's level (+0.007 vs. original, p = 0.65; all other comparisons non-significant, see Figure 11 and3) (an inference)1.
Round 3: the fine-tuned model sets the recipe

When the Round-1 fine-tuned model took over designing the Round-3 recipe, its first two responses exhausted the 8,192-token output cap while thinking and returned empty bodies, producing a valid recipe only on the third try (whereas the original model succeeded on its first try in Rounds 1 and 2)1. It kept Round 1's aggressive settings almost intact, adding only a 1% minimum relative-gain threshold to select 539 calls1.

Yet the resulting Round-3 model dropped sharply to 0.392—significantly worse than Round 2 (−0.204, 95% CI [−0.365, −0.065], p = 0.008), the original model (−0.197, 95% CI [−0.363, −0.050], p = 0.031), Round 1 (−0.213, p = 0.047), and the fixed recipe (−0.145, p = 0.008), with the steepest drops against the random recipe on sequence reversal (−0.48) and modular addition (−0.34) (Figure 13)3,1.
This outcome highlights two findings:

items: Recipe and training intensity shaped the outcome: Retraining the Round-1 recipe with a new random seed scored 0.602, close to the original 0.605. This rules out ordinary seed variation as the explanation for the Round-1 to Round-3 gap. Qwen3.8-27B used the Round-3 data filter with lighter training and scored 0.513, above Round 3 at 0.392 but below the original model at 0.588. Across the four recipes, data selection and training intensity both affected successor performance.

Behavioral collapse from training intensity: All three heavily trained models (Round 1, Round 3, and Round 3's random-recipe control) shifted on unseen tasks to firing thousands of very short calls (11,287–15,087 calls, median 47–54 tokens) compared to 2,030 calls (median 111 tokens) for the original model and 101 tokens for the lightly trained Round-2 model—demonstrating that this behavioral shift stems from training intensity rather than who designed the recipe (an inference)1.

en.html: Continuing from the best version

Besides unseen tasks, another way to prevent a successor from simply replaying memorized training answers is to have every improver continue from the same frontier checkpoint—specifically, the best NanoChat version (1.2308) found during our first-order run119,1. Four improvers each ran 3 single-threaded 12-attempt continuations with rotated evaluation GPUs, measured by the loss drop from each run's own re-measured baseline (1.2285–1.2353)1,126:

Across 3 runs per group, run-to-run spread within a single improver (e.g., 0.0005 to 0.0243 for the original model) exceeded the differences between improvers; when continuing from the same frontier version, neither a successor model nor the lessons note yielded a measurable speedup (an inference)1,126.

en.html: All reported 9B groups were checked for truncated model calls. The audit found no systematic truncation that would alter the comparisons. Improvement scores and statistical tests followed the task-paired analysis specified in advance1,127.
Follow-up test: recipe effects and seed variation

Round 3 scored substantially below Round 1. Two follow-up comparisons tested whether the difference reflected training randomness or the recipe designer. The first kept Round 1's data and recipe fixed and changed only the LoRA random seed. The second used Qwen3.8-27B as the recipe designer, with the same feedback given to the original model in Round 2.

head: Comparison
Difference
95% CI

rows: Round-1 recipe retrained with a new seed − original Round-1 model

en.html: The new-seed run scored 0.602, close to Round 1's 0.605. The gap between Rounds 1 and 3 therefore cannot be attributed to random-seed variation. The Qwen3.8-27B-designed recipe scored 0.513. It outperformed Round 3 but did not surpass the original or Round-2 model1,5.

Across the four recipes, two choices tracked the outcome: whether accepted records with small gains were removed, and training intensity. On the same 539 records, lighter training scored 0.513 and heavier training scored 0.392. The two Round-1 runs that retained all records scored 0.605 and 0.602. These comparisons show that recipe choices shaped successor performance, while they do not isolate the causal contribution of each choice1,5.
Limitations

items: Limited generational horizon and scale: Successors were tracked for only three generations, and self-designed recipes for three rounds (with a single round of feedback from training tasks). Only one base model (Qwen3.5-9B) was tested across fast micro-tasks and one NanoChat task (whose sealed-data endpoint verification remains pending)1.

Cross-task variance vs. statistical power: While the A/A minimum detectable effect is about 0.031, differences between distinct models fluctuated widely across tasks (−0.58 to +0.35), requiring larger true effects for detection; the continue-from-best experiment was likewise limited to 3 runs per arm1,122.

Single-run recipe variance and human-bounded recipe space: Each self-designed recipe was trained only once (Rounds 1 and 3 used nearly identical recipes that stopped at ~2.4 and ~2.7 epochs under the 55-minute cap yet differed in score by 0.213), making single-run recipe comparisons unreliable (an inference)3,1. Moreover, because the model selected only from predefined options rather than writing arbitrary training code, the setup remains within GPI rather than RSI under Tang et al.'s criterion8,1.

Serving-path confound: The original model was served directly by vLLM without an adapter, whereas all fine-tuned checkpoints were routed through vLLM's LoRA adapter path; this confound affects only comparisons against the original model, leaving comparisons among successors and against placebos unaffected122.

zh.html: 经验笔记：自由文本的经验会拖慢改进

挂载经验笔记后，原始模型的改进速度分从 0.588 降至 0.392，比未查阅任何记录写出的通用建议还低 0.2393。无外部真值校验的自由文本反思与记忆堆积在多项研究中表现出同样的退化。ExpeL 在提取经验时引入自我反思后，HotpotQA 成功率从 39.0 降至 29.0128。缺乏外部真值参照时，GPT-4 在 GSM8K 上经过两轮自我纠错后准确率从 95.5 降至 89.0129，Reflexion 在 MBPP Python 上的表现也从 0.80 降至 0.77130。在上下文维护层面，ACE 整体重写上下文时触发了上下文坍缩（context collapse），准确率从 66.7 跌至 57.1，低于不做任何适应的基线 63.7131。Xiong 等人允许 agent 无筛选地累积记忆后，全部四个被测 agent 的表现均低于固定记忆基线（例如从 67.53 降至 55.48）132。

文献中经验机制产生正收益的案例，均依赖严格的外部过滤或形式化约束。Sarukkai 等人仅保留成功轨迹并按相似度检索，将 ALFWorld 成功率从 73% 提升至 89%133。Voyager 则仅存储通过自我验证的可执行技能代码134。归纳而言，经验机制生效需要满足三个条件之一：由可靠的外部信号过滤条目、测试任务与所存经验同分布，或存储对象为已验证的可执行产物114。第 4 节的经验笔记不满足上述任何一条。它是模型自由生成的未过滤文本，且直接迁移至未见过的任务类型。笔记中“忽略任何哪怕略微增加损失的改动”这一规则直接锁死了探索空间，与 ACE 记录的误导性信号污染上下文属于同一机制推断1,131。
图 18 加入自我反思、经验或记忆之后，表现相对原来变化了多少。各研究的任务和指标不同（成功率、准确率、改进速度分），这里只比较相对变化的方向和幅度。橙色是变差，蓝色是变好。Xiong 等人有四个 agent，画成四个点128,129,131,132,130,133,3。

zh.html: 成功记录与失败记录训练出的模型没有差别

第一代后继模型使用被采纳的成功记录微调，安慰剂模型使用等量的被否决记录微调，两者在未见任务上的改进速度分仅相差 +0.004（p = 0.91）3。这一结果与 Spurious Rewards 的发现直接对应：在 MATH-500 上对 Qwen2.5-Math-7B 进行强化学习时，真实奖励带来 29.1 个百分点的提升，纯随机奖励也能带来 21.4 个百分点的提升135。该研究指出，训练后模型调用代码推理的比例从约 65% 升至 90% 以上，说明收益源于激活模型固有的行为模式，而非学到了奖励信号本身的内容135。Mind the Gap 同样发现，部分模型首轮自我改进的表观提升仅源于输出格式更加规范17。Sharpening 则从理论上证明，自我改进只能将概率质量集中到模型原本就能生成的输出分布上，无法创造基座模型不具备的信息136。
这组证据指向同一结论：在当前实验规模下，LoRA 微调仅改变了模型的表面调用习惯，并未赋予模型甄别“哪些研究假设有效”的判断力推断。本报告引入“失败尝试记录微调”作为安慰剂对照以剥离这一混杂因素，在检索到的文献中尚无先例114。
三代后继模型：没有加速，第三代变差

在人类预设的固定循环内反复自我训练，文献中的一阶任务得分普遍在数轮内饱和或回退。Mind the Gap 测得生成与验证的差距在两至三轮内降至接近 017。SPIN 经过四轮迭代，平均分从初始的 58.14 依次升至 60.80、62.12、62.97 和 63.16，单轮增量逐次衰减18。ReST-EM 在 APPS 上的收益集中在第一轮，继续迭代便出现回退19。Self-Rewarding 虽然在 AlpacaEval 胜率上连续三轮上升，但同期 GSM8K 准确率从 60.27 降至 57.70，输出长度则从 1092 膨胀至 2552 token137。
图 19 固定循环下的自我训练逐轮表现。前三幅是文献中的结果，各自用论文报告的指标；最后一幅是本报告三代后继模型在未见过任务上的改进速度分。文献中的曲线在被优化的指标上上升、增量递减；本报告测的是“当改进者的速度”，三代都没有超过原始模型18,138,137,3。

zh.html: 当测量指标从一阶任务得分转向二阶改进速度时，三代后继模型均未超过原始模型。补充实验进一步显示，第一轮配方换种子重训后得分保持稳定，而第三轮的下降与其数据筛选和训练强度有关3,5。Shumailov 等人将递归训练退化归因于自生成数据导致输出分布尾部逐代消失124，而 Gerstgrasser 等人证明将新生成数据累积在原始真实数据之上（而非替换原始数据）可规避此类分布坍缩139。本实验每一代均从原始权重重新初始化，并采用包含了原始模型全部记录的累积数据集进行训练122。本实验中，跨代改进速度未能提升。结果与自生成数据导致的经典模型坍缩有所不同，因为每一代均从原始权重重新初始化，并累积使用原始模型记录；本实验没有测量输出分布尾部，因此不对两者的机制作等同判断。
让模型自己决定怎么训练自己

SEAL 允许模型自主生成微调数据与超参数，在经过外层强化学习训练后，其在 ARC 子集上的自我编辑成功率从未经训练时的 20% 提升至 72.5%125。第 4 节的配方设计者并未经历外层强化学习训练，仅接收过一次源自训练任务的单轮反馈1。第一轮盲定配方（0.605）与第二轮引入反馈后的配方（0.595），均未与原始模型（0.588）拉开统计显著差距3。这表明 SEAL 的正收益依赖于外层强化学习对“生成配方”这一元能力的专门训练，仅靠预训练模型自身的零样本或单次反馈决策无法选出更优的训练配方推断。

第三轮交由第一轮微调后的模型接管配方设计，所得模型的改进速度分暴跌至 0.3923。这一退化印证了文献中的两项规律。首先，STOP 发现只有当底层模型为 GPT-4 时，改进者改写自身代码才能带来正收益，换用 GPT-3.5 或 Mixtral 时均会发生退化29。其次，HGM 证明模型在当前任务上的一阶得分与其繁衍优秀后代的元生产力之间仅呈弱相关（加权 Pearson 相关系数为 0.285 至 0.444）111。第一轮模型在训练任务上的一阶得分虽高于原始模型（0.652 对 0.525），但它设计的下一次更新却导致严重退化，在模型权重层面直接证实了“下游任务表现更好”不等于“更擅长改进自身”推断1,3。
与已有二阶测量和回报率模型的关系

在模型权重层面，此前文献中尚无直接测量二阶改进速度的先例114。脚手架层面的 AIDE² ignition test 测得改进后教练与人工教练的得分为 0.780 对 0.782，作者判定为无显著差异（"we find these results to be inconclusive"）20。DGM 的消融实验显示，移除自我改进机制会使 SWE-bench 和 Polyglot 的终点得分从 50.0 和 38.0 降至 39.0 和 28.0，说明让被改进的 agent 亲自执行下一轮修改能带来额外收益，但并未报告代际改进速度的提升110。第 4 节将二阶测试推进至模型权重层面，得出了明确的零结果：三代之内未发生代际加速。

在宏观增长模型中，Epoch 与 Forethought 使用研发回报率 r 刻画软件效率是否加速（当 r > 1 时效率翻倍所需时间逐次缩短）15,16。既有估计主要基于人类研发的历史轨迹，例如图像识别的中位数为 1.4（0.8 至 2.4），国际象棋引擎约为 0.83，Forethought 在固定算力下的综合估计为 0.5 至 216,15。本实验测量的是固定预算下各代改进者的速度差值，与按累积研发投入定义的 r 在量纲上不能直接换算；同时，Davidson 与 Houlden 的理论模型同样预测系统逼近能力上限时回报率将回落，因此三代之内的零结果并不排除更长周期或更大规模下出现 r > 1 的可能推断31。
小结
在本报告的检索范围内，本报告首次在模型权重层面建立了二阶改进的直接测量基线。通过将微调后的后继模型放回改进者位置，并配齐 A/A 噪声标定、失败记录安慰剂与同量数据/随机配方三类严格对照，实验证实：上下文经验总结会因搜索空间收窄而拖慢改进，轨迹微调仅改变调用行为而未习得有效的研究判断，固定循环在三代之内即出现退化，且交由微调后的后继模型接管下一次更新配方会导致表现显著恶化3,114。
